proposals.after: (Conversational Garden: When he heard of his father's death, Dao set out on foot by starlight while his family hurried after with a bag of clothes and overtook him.)

proposals.after: (Tan Yuan, Conversational Garden: On hearing of his father's death, Dao set out on foot by starlight. His family followed behind with a bag of clothes and caught up with him.)
proposals.reason: English retains a stray Chinese annotation closer that is not part of the translation.

proposals.before: Li Qi, a Liang chief minister, also prided himself on his prose. He once submitted a memorial on pacifying Zhongshan and Wang Du that read, "The rebel of Zhending is recovered."
proposals.after: Li Qi, a Liang chief minister, also prided himself on his prose. He once submitted a memorial congratulating the pacification of Wang Du of Zhongshan that read, "The rebel of Zhending is recovered."
proposals.reason: The title 賀平中山王都表 names Wang Du of Zhongshan, not Zhongshan and Wang Du as two separate objects.

proposals.before: There was also Li Qi, a chief minister of the Liang, who always prided himself on his literary skill. He once submitted a memorial congratulating the pacification of Zhongshan and Wang Du, saying, "We have recovered the rebel of Zhending."
proposals.after: There was also Li Qi, a chief minister of the Liang, who always prided himself on his literary skill. He once submitted a memorial congratulating the pacification of Wang Du of Zhongshan, saying, "We have recovered the rebel of Zhending."
proposals.reason: 中山王都 is Wang Du of Zhongshan; splitting it as Zhongshan and Wang Du misreads the memorial title.

proposals.before: (Conversational Garden: Dao and the other chief ministers returned to the Secretariat. After eating, a clerk of the outer hall came forward and told Dao about the northern mission.)
proposals.after: (Yang Neihan's Conversational Garden: Dao and the other chief ministers returned to the Secretariat. After eating, a clerk of the outer hall came forward and told Dao about the northern mission.)
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 楊內翰, the named author of the cited note.

proposals.before: The Khitan ruler was delighted and quietly urged him to stay. Dao said, "The southern court is my son, the northern my father—yet I am subject to both. What difference is there?"
proposals.after: The Khitan ruler was delighted and quietly urged him to stay. Dao said, "The southern court is the son, the northern court the father—yet I am subject to both courts. What difference is there?"
proposals.reason: 南朝為子，北朝為父 describes the two courts' diplomatic father-son relation, not Dao's own filiation; 'my son/my father' invents that.

proposals.before: Soon he was made Grand Mentor and concurrent Palace Attendant and advanced to Duke of Lu.
proposals.after: Soon he was made Minister of Education (Situ) and concurrent Palace Attendant and advanced to Duke of Lu.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is Situ (Minister of Education / Minister over the Masses), not Grand Mentor (太傅).

proposals.before: Shortly afterward he was made Grand Mentor and concurrent Palace Attendant, advanced to Duke of Lu.
proposals.after: Shortly afterward he was made Minister of Education (Situ) and concurrent Palace Attendant, advanced to Duke of Lu.
proposals.reason: Same office error as the idiomatic line: 司徒 is not Grand Mentor.

proposals.before: At the time the commissioners of the Three Departments were in power; in the seats of government all except the Prince of Yingzhou hated him and said, "How can a prefectural commissioner dare oppose an imperial edict of the court!
proposals.after: At the time the commissioners of the Three Departments were in power; in the seats of government all except the Prince of Ying hated him and said, "How can a prefectural commissioner dare oppose an imperial edict of the court!
proposals.reason: 瀛王 is the title Prince of Ying, not Yingzhou.

proposals.before: Before the edict was issued, the Prince of Yingzhou alone requested an audience at an irregular hour.
proposals.after: Before the edict was issued, the Prince of Ying alone requested an audience at an irregular hour.
proposals.reason: Chinese 瀛王 is Prince of Ying, not Prince of Yingzhou.

proposals.before: When the Han founder came out, the Prince of Yingzhou said, "When Your Majesty was in Hedong, prohibiting ox hides was fitting; now that you possess the realm, hides ought not to be banned.
proposals.after: When the Han founder came out, the Prince of Ying said, "When Your Majesty was in Hedong, prohibiting ox hides was fitting; now that you possess the realm, hides ought not to be banned.
proposals.reason: Chinese 瀛王 is Prince of Ying, not Prince of Yingzhou.

proposals.before: The Prince of Yingzhou said, "The edict has not yet been issued."
proposals.after: The Prince of Ying said, "The edict has not yet been issued."
proposals.reason: Chinese 瀛王 is Prince of Ying, not Prince of Yingzhou.

proposals.before: When the Khitan held Bian I was held by the northern ruler; from Zhenzhou I returned to Han with officials and troops and now serve Gaozu and the present emperor.
proposals.after: When the Khitan held Bian, I was held by the northern ruler; from Zhenzhou I returned to Han with officials and troops and now serve Gaozu and the present emperor.
proposals.reason: Missing comma after Bian fuses the place Bian with the subject I, yielding the false proper names Bian I and Zhenzhou I.

proposals.before: My ranks ran from Gentleman for Merit through court grand master titles to Special Advancement and Grand General with the Ceremonies of the Three Dukes.
proposals.after: My ranks ran from Gentleman for Merit through court grand master titles to Special Advancement and Unrivaled in Honor with the Ceremonies of the Three Ducal Ministers.
proposals.reason: 開府儀同三司 is a prestige rank equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, not a Grand General.

proposals.before: My ranks ran from Gentleman for Merit to Grand Master for Court Discussion, Grand Master for Court Assembly, Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal, Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Gold Seal, Special Advancement, and Grand General with the Ceremonies of the Three Dukes.
proposals.after: My ranks ran from Gentleman for Merit to Grand Master for Court Discussion, Grand Master for Court Assembly, Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal, Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Gold Seal, Special Advancement, and Unrivaled in Honor with the Ceremonies of the Three Ducal Ministers.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 開府儀同三司 as Grand General in the literal field.

proposals.before: My regular offices ran from Secretariat drafting secretary to twice Vice Minister of Revenue, then Vice Ministers of War and Secretariat, Vice Director of the Chancellery, Ministers of Justice and Personnel, and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; thrice Minister of Works; then Grand Mentor with Palace Attendant, sixteen halberds for my gate, Grand Commandant with Palace Attendant, Khitan Grand Tutor, and Han Grand Preceptor.
proposals.after: My regular offices ran from Secretariat drafting secretary to twice Vice Minister of Revenue, then Vice Ministers of War and Secretariat, Vice Director of the Chancellery, Ministers of Justice and Personnel, and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; thrice Minister of Works, twice in the Secretariat and once keeping the original office; then Grand Mentor with Palace Attendant, sixteen halberds for my gate, Grand Commandant with Palace Attendant, Khitan Grand Tutor, and Han Grand Preceptor.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 兩在中書，一守本官, which the Chinese and literal both record.

proposals.before: My eldest daughter married Xuan, son of the deceased Vice Minister of War Cui Yan and Vice Director of the Imperial Stud, and was enfeoffed as Lady of Wannian County;
proposals.after: My eldest daughter married Xuan, son of the deceased Vice Minister of War Cui Yan; Xuan was Vice Director of the Imperial Stud, and she was enfeoffed as Lady of Wannian County;
proposals.reason: The Chinese makes 太僕少卿 modify 絢, not Cui Yan; the literal conjunction fuses Xuan's office onto the father.

proposals.before: Erect no spirit-way stele, for the ancients set none at the tomb.
proposals.after: Erect no spirit-way stele, because in the Three Dynasties none was set before the tomb.
proposals.reason: 三代 names the Three Dynasties, not generic ancients already used for 古人 in s0191.

proposals.before: The essays and poems I wrote, apart from many lost in the press of affairs, are gathered into a family collection those I could recover. Whether those who see my intent and know me, or those who condemn me, are many or few, I do not know.
proposals.after: The essays and poems I wrote, apart from many lost in the press of affairs, those I could recover are gathered into a family collection. Whether those who see my intent and know me, or those who condemn me, are many or few, I do not know.
proposals.reason: English grammar breaks after 'family collection'.

proposals.before: Thus ends the preface of the Old Man of Everlasting Joy, dated Qianyou 3.
proposals.after: Thus ends the preface of the Old Man of Everlasting Joy, dated the Zhu-ming month of Qianyou 3.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits the date element 朱明月 preserved in the Chinese and literal.

proposals.before: Feng Ji, son of the Prince of Yingzhou Feng Dao, could play the pipa with leather strings. Shizong once had him play before the throne and greatly admired it, therefore naming his pipa "Thunder Rolling Round the Hall."
proposals.after: Feng Ji, son of Prince of Ying Feng Dao, could play the pipa with leather strings. Shizong once had him play before the throne and greatly admired it, therefore naming his pipa "Thunder Rolling Round the Hall."
proposals.reason: 瀛王道 is Feng Dao as Prince of Ying; Yingzhou over-translates 瀛.

decisions.reason: The idiomatic English ends with a leftover Chinese annotation closer 〉 after the English parenthesis; that mark belongs only to the Chinese note wrappers, not to the translation.

decisions.reason: 賀平中山王都表 is a memorial congratulating the pacification of Wang Du of Zhongshan; reading 中山 and 王都 as two separate objects is a misparse of the title.
The same title 賀平中山王都表 names Wang Du of Zhongshan, not Zhongshan and Wang Du as coordinate objects of pacification.
The Chinese citation is 楊內翰《談苑》; the idiomatic line omitted the named author 楊內翰 that the source attributes.
南朝為子，北朝為父 names the two courts as son and father in diplomatic hierarchy; 兩朝皆為臣 is Dao’s dual subjecthood. ‘My son/my father’ invents personal filiation the Chinese does not state.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 南朝為子，北朝為父，兩朝皆為臣

decisions.reason: The office granted is 司徒, not 太傅; Grand Mentor is the wrong title, and Minister of Education (Situ) restores the source office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 尋加司徒、兼侍中，進魯國公

decisions.reason: The literal field repeats the same error: 司徒 is Situ, not Grand Mentor.
The source title is 馮瀛王, Prince of Ying; Yingzhou adds 州, which the Chinese here does not write.
獨瀛王 is the Prince of Ying, not Prince of Yingzhou.
The speaker is 瀛王, Prince of Ying; Yingzhou is an invented place-title.
馮瀛王 is again Prince of Ying; the literal Yingzhou over-translates 瀛.
契丹據汴京，為北主所制 separates the occupation of Bianjing from the first-person detainee; without a comma, Bian I reads as a false name. The added comma restores the clause break.

decisions.after: My ranks ran from Gentleman for Merit through court grand master titles to Special Advancement and Grand Master Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
decisions.reason: 開府儀同三司 is a prestige rank, not a Grand General, but ‘Unrivaled in Honor with the Ceremonies of the Three Ducal Ministers’ awkwardly stacks two renderings of the same title. Grand Master Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers is the accurate complete English.

decisions.after: My ranks ran from Gentleman for Merit to Grand Master for Court Discussion, Grand Master for Court Assembly, Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal, Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Gold Seal, Special Advancement, and Grand Master Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
decisions.reason: The literal field has the same real error (Grand General for 開府儀同三司), but the proposed hybrid English is still awkward; use Grand Master Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

decisions.after: My regular offices ran from Secretariat drafting secretary to twice Vice Minister of Revenue, then Vice Ministers of War and Secretariat, Vice Director of the Chancellery, Ministers of Justice and Personnel, and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; thrice Minister of Works, twice in the Secretariat and once keeping the original office; then Minister of Education (Situ) with Palace Attendant, sixteen halberds for my gate, Grand Commandant with Palace Attendant, Khitan Grand Tutor, and Han Grand Preceptor.
decisions.reason: The idiomatic line does omit 兩在中書，一守本官, which must be restored, but the proposed after still renders 又授司徒 as Grand Mentor. 司徒 is Situ, not 太傅.

decisions.after: Feng Ji, son of the Prince of Ying Feng Dao, could play the pipa with leather strings. Shizong once had him play before the throne and greatly admired it, therefore naming his pipa "Thunder Rolling Round the Hall."
decisions.reason: 瀛王道 is Feng Dao as Prince of Ying, so Yingzhou is wrong, but dropping the article from ‘the Prince of Yingzhou’ leaves ‘son of Prince of Ying Feng Dao’ awkward. Keep the article while correcting the title.
